demand_zones.zone_name: Toy demand zone (representative Melbourne metropolitan supply region)

provenance.task: 4. Research and select the toy-model demand value

final_value.confirmed_by: Optimisation team, official AquaBlend toy-model configuration

derivation.method_note: 500 ML/day is a confirmed configuration input, not derived bottom-up. The published total per-capita rate is used in reverse to record the served population the confirmed value implies, so the value carries a traceable basis in published data.
derivation.forward_check: 242 L/person/day x 2,066,000 people = 499,972,000 L/day = about 500 ML/day

implied_population_justification.ground_1_real_world_anchor: About 2,066,000 is a major metropolitan supply region, not one council area: roughly 39 percent of Greater Melbourne's 5.3 million, equivalent to about twelve mid-sized LGAs (metropolitan average about 171,000 across 31 LGAs; City of Monash 209,268 and City of Whitehorse 183,462 at 30 June 2024). A regional zone is the scale consistent with the confirmed source set, since Silvan is a principal distribution point rather than a local storage and the Yarra extraction and production bore are likewise system-scale inputs with capacities in the hundreds of ML/day.
implied_population_justification.ground_2_calibration_window: At 242 L/person/day the toy is only non-trivial for demand above the largest single confirmed capacity (350 ML/day) and no greater than the total (710 ML/day), which corresponds to a population above about 1,446,000 and up to about 2,934,000. The confirmed 500 ML/day and its implied 2,066,000 sit inside that band with room on both sides.
implied_population_justification.note: Representative regional zone size, not a measured Melbourne Water service area boundary.
implied_population_justification.supersedes: Earlier version derived 50 ML/day from an assumed single-LGA population of 207,000. That derivation suited the provisional reservoir-only capacities and no longer applies.

confirmed_toy_source_set.source_types: mixed (surface storage, river extraction, groundwater). The toy is no longer reservoir-only.
confirmed_toy_source_set.note: Large / mid / small trio. Both silvan_reservoir and yarra_kew are structurally required in every feasible solution; groundwater_bore_1 is not needed in the baseline and only activates under stress, exercising the binary activation logic.

calibration.note: 350 < 500 and 710 >= 500, so both rules hold on the confirmed values. Demand and capacities are mutually consistent and ready for Task 5 hand validation.
calibration.supersedes: Earlier provisional calibration against assumed caps of 40, 25 and 5 ML/day at a demand of 50 ML/day.

sources.note: Used only to give scale to the implied toy demand-zone population. City of Monash 209,268; City of Whitehorse 183,462.

notes: required_volume_ML of 500 is a confirmed configuration value from the Optimisation team, not a value selected in this task.
required_volume_ML is expressed on a total per-capita basis (residential + business + system losses), consistent with the total daily_usage_ML series.

implied_population of 2,066,000 is a reconciliation of the confirmed demand against published per-capita demand, not a measured demand zone. Justification is recorded under derivation.implied_population_justification.
Confirmed source set: silvan_reservoir, yarra_kew, groundwater_bore_1. Mixed source types, not reservoir-only.

Daily-extractable capacities of 350, 300 and 60 ML/day are confirmed configuration inputs, not published Melbourne Water safe-yield figures. No independent public capacity figure exists for yarra_kew or groundwater_bore_1 in the datasets used.
Both calibration rules hold against the confirmed capacities.

Supersedes the earlier version of this file: demand 50 ML/day, sources Sugarloaf / Silvan / O'Shannassy, provisional caps 40 / 25 / 5 ML/day, assumed population 207,000. The earlier reservoir-only source-selection analysis, including the exclusion of Thomson and Upper Yarra and the resolution of Barawon and Yashai127 as monitoring station identifiers, no longer applies.
